scope: Viewed source batch79 v2, both final native images and final nearest-8x comparison; independently measured pixels, replayed pixel logs and reran inspected author script into /tmp/sela-independent-rebuild. Original concept files and pilot PNGs not modified.
visual_findings: B preferred for this bounded experiment: pale sleeve and shirt clusters, teal cape, separated boots and hollow rope loop remain readable at native size; A now retains a closed loop but crowds it against the right-hand silhouette and trouser edge.

Both retain the brown bun, trailing hair strand, teal shoulder cape, oatmeal sleeves, grey-brown trousers, brown boots and belt, and one rope loop. Empty hands and civilian identity remain; no armor, weapon or Verren facial features were introduced.
Both have visibly hard stepped outlines and coherent flat colors. B has more stable hand/cuff and rope-hole separation; A sacrifices facial and clothing nuance to its smaller grid.

Large head, conspicuous face and simplified adult proportions remain a stylized concept choice; neither experiment demonstrates exact Stoneshard anatomy or information density. Visual preference is not inferred from passing numeric checks.

The surviving one-pixel hair strand and narrow rope segments are legitimate details, not noise. No disconnected alpha singleton was removed by the sampler in either result; the recorded B hand-contour removal changes only one pixel below the mitten.
Foot-anchor x is a canvas alignment datum between the legs, not necessarily an opaque pixel or real engine origin. Lowest visible rows are verified at 45 and 61; origins and collision remain unknown.
failure_conditions: Any soft alpha or unrecorded color would fail the binary-alpha/palette study.
Loss of bun, cape, rope-loop hole, adult/civilian identity, or damage to intentional narrow details would fail visual identity despite numeric compliance.
Treating these two chosen canvases or anchors as verified engine specifications would exceed the evidence.
Formal native import still requires matched-version NPC metadata, direction/state conventions and in-game standing/occlusion/click/collision verification.

visual_findings: C meets the one-reference 34px visible-height budget while approximately retaining source aspect ratio. Bun, teal cape, pale sleeves, grey-brown trousers and separated brown boots remain identifiable.

At 1x, the rope reads as a small ochre attachment; at 8x its two-pixel dark interior is visible. Rolled-cuff and rope-material detail is reduced. Bun has a narrow hair tip but face/hair clusters are more cramped.

B remains the clearest identity/readability study, aided by its substantially larger visible height. C is a fairer height-budget comparison to the single Verren reference, not an equivalent-quality or game-compatible sprite.
The numerical budget pass does not prove authentic original-game anatomy or style; keep C as an alternative, not an engine specification.
